parsed.explanation: Traveller-facing exposures are mostly absent. No trans-specific offence, no border or facility restriction, and bathroom access is protected. The dossier records no birth-sex ward or custody rule for visitors, though custody and ward practice are not explicitly documented. Discrimination law covers gender identity in services and employment, and a 2023 trans killing ended in a 12-year sentence with the provocation claim rejected. Social attitudes are split, with younger people markedly more accepting. Deductions: no hate-crime or hate-speech coverage of gender identity, so recourse is thin; the 2024 avoidance figures (40% avoid locations for fear of assault) are LGBTIQ-wide rather than trans-specific, so they carry little weight; the 2023 assault and 2007 Pride attacks show some hostility; and the record conflicts on whether trans killings are documented. Overall, a reduced-risk profile with documented acceptance and a prosecuted trans killing, held below the top tier by the recourse gap and unresolved custody and ward questions.
